MSI Afterburner is the known and trusted monitor/tweak utitlity for GPU's that has the ugliest and most outdated UI in existence - but it's what, I assume, the vast majority of people and myself use with their GPU's.

Well, my Zotac GTX 1080 could only ever get a stable OC on MSI Afterburner at around +100 Core and +150 Mem.

Saw a thing on the interwebs about using Firestorm for Zotac GPU's, seeing that since it was literally made for them, I downloaded it and, well...

Full breakdown:

GPU Clock: +241 MHz (2000 MHz @ boost)

GPU Max Volt: +20%

Memory Clock +500 MHz

Power: 120%

GPU Temp Target: 92c (OCCT burner tests plateaud at around 73c)

- Completely stable -

Now, the reason why I added the (or both) at the end of the title is that if, like me, you use Rainmeter for desktop system monitors, they almost all use MSI Afterburner for their sensor data. However, as long as you apply your OC in Firestorm and then DON'T touch it in Afterburner, they'll play nice together without messing anything up - atleast, as far as I can tell.

Edit: Quick addendum, FIrestorm's UI is almost the exact same as Afterburner's so it looks just as much like ass as Afterburner.
If you have a Zotac GPU you might want to use Firestorm instead of MSI Afterburner (or both)
